name: Cornrows
summary: Continuous raised braids worked directly against the scalp in straight or curved rows.
intro: Cornrow braiding originated in Africa. Hair is added into each braid as it advances along a parted lane, producing a raised ridge fixed close to the scalp.
The parting pattern controls the direction of the design. Parallel rows read cleanly from front to back, while curved parts guide the braids into a sweep.

variations.name: Straight-back cornrows
variations.description: Parallel lanes run from the front hairline toward the nape.

variations.name: Curved cornrows
variations.description: The rows follow shaped parts that arc around the crown or to one side.

variations.name: Feed-in cornrows
variations.description: Added hair is incorporated gradually when extra length or fullness is wanted.

consultation.intro: Agree on the row layout, width and finish before braiding. Bring a photo that shows the pattern from above.
questions: How many rows and what spacing would you like?
Should the ends be tucked, tied, or left hanging?
Would you like the braids made entirely from your own hair?
consultation.sampleRequest: “I’d like raised straight-back rows with visible parts, a comfortable hairline, and the ends secured neatly at the nape.”

considerations: Tell the braider if a section hurts or feels too tight. Repeated pull at the same spots can contribute to traction hair loss.
The starting length and density affect how narrow a braid can be and how securely the ends can be finished.
